public_rationale: The research documents a large prospective buildout, but does not establish this claim’s particular revenue requirement. Construction cost is not customer revenue, and a forecast of additions through 2030 includes more than facilities already under construction in August 2026. A supported numerical judgment would require assumptions that the claim and retrieved evidence do not supply.
limitations: The cited industry forecast is context only.
This assessment concerns an asserted economic requirement, not whether future demand eventually appears.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Monetizing the data center capacity under construction requires hundreds of billions of dollars of demand in the next few years.

statement.excerpt: Based on the amount under construction, we need — even with OpenAI and Anthropic — hundreds of billions of dollars’ worth of demand in the next few years just to monetize the data center capacity under construction.

from_speaker: Based on the amount under construction
hundreds of billions of dollars’ worth of demand
our_interpretation: This states a present economic requirement for the construction pipeline, rather than predicting that the demand will arrive.
Assess the facilities under construction on August 11, 2026.
Hundreds of billions means at least $200 billion, including demand from the two labs.
Monetize ordinarily means obtain revenue from the capacity. It does not by itself specify full investment recovery, profitability or a target return.
Do not silently convert the unspecified demand total into annual revenue or assign an exact deadline to the next few years.
criteria.support_condition: A reproducible model of the facilities already under construction shows that monetizing that capacity over the stated near-term period requires at least $200 billion of customer spending under clearly specified pricing and utilization assumptions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A comparable model of the same construction cohort shows that its monetization requires materially less than $200 billion under reasonable assumptions.

evidence.explanation: JLL's dated forecast establishes the scale of its projected global expansion. It does not isolate facilities under construction on August 11 or calculate the customer revenue required to monetize them.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A transparent model for the August 11 construction cohort, with a defined monetization test, time period, prices and utilization, showing whether required customer spending reaches $200 billion.
